title: Do you need to declutter your home?
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. Do you live in a neat and tidy home?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是乔治,你住的很整洁吗?

sentences.en: Or is there stuff everywhere? If your room is filled with heaps of clothes and piles of books, you may have a problem with clutter – things in your home which take up space in an untidy, disorganised way.
sentences.zh: 或者到处都有东西吗?如果你的房间满是衣物和书,你可能会对杂乱无章的东西有问题,这些东西在你的家里以混乱和无组织的方式占据了空间。

sentences.en: Clutter is a common problem. In fact, clutter was the topic of a recent episode of BBC Radio 4 programme, Woman's Hour.
sentences.zh: Clutter是一个常见的问题。 事实上,杂乱无章是英国广播公司第四电台节目“妇女一小时”的最近一集的主题。

sentences.en: Here's presenter Nuala McGovern reading a message from one listener: Some of you have been in touch already to share your thoughts and experiences when it comes to clutter.
sentences.zh: 这位是主持人努阿拉·麦戈文,他读到一位听众的讯息:你们中有些人已经联系过,想在混乱中分享你们的想法和经验。

sentences.en: Here is one: "The clutter in my house is actually starting to affect my mental health.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个: “我家里的杂乱无章的人 开始影响我的心理健康。

sentences.en: I can't think or work anymore, so much so it woke me at 4 a.m. this morning and I felt a strong urge to tidy.
sentences.zh: 我无法思考或工作了,所以今早4点把我吵醒了 我强烈要求整洁

sentences.en: I have given myself a week as I cannot take it anymore."
sentences.zh: 我给自己一周,因为我再也受不了了。”

sentences.en: So, Neil, do you have a problem with clutter?
sentences.zh: 尼尔,你对杂乱无章有意见吗?

sentences.en: Well, I don't have a problem with clutter, but I live with children and there is clutter everywhere, and it drives me mad.
sentences.zh: 我对杂乱无章 但我和孩子住在一起 到处都是杂乱无章 这让我很生气

sentences.en: Oh, that's so annoying. How about you? Yeah, I don't have a problem with clutter.
sentences.zh: 哦,真烦人 你呢?

sentences.en: I would describe myself as a minimalist.
sentences.zh: 我会把自己描述成一个最起码的人

sentences.en: I don't have very much stuff. Ah, very efficient!
sentences.zh: 我没有什么东西,很有效率!

sentences.en: Yes. So, we don't have a problem with clutter, but if you do, there's a simple solution: decluttering – or throwing away some of the unused stuff filling our homes.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以,我们没有问题 杂乱无章,但如果你有, 有一个简单的解决方案: 消沉 — 或者扔掉一些未用的东西 填满了我们的家。

sentences.en: But deciding what to keep and what to throw away is not so easy, so in this episode we'll hear some advice on keeping your life clutter-free, along with some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 但决定要保留什么和丢掉什么并不容易, 所以在这个插曲中,我们会听到一些建议, 让你的生活保持无忧无虑, 以及一些有用的新词句。

sentences.en: And remember, you can find all the vocabulary for this programme, along with a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 并记住,你可以找到这个节目的所有词汇, 连同一个测验和工作表, 在我们的网站,bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但首先 我有个问题要问你 乔治

sentences.en: Decluttering was popularised by Marie Kondo's best-selling 2011 book, The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up, and there's still lots of interest today.
sentences.zh: Marie Kondo最畅销的2011年书《倾斜的改变生命的魔法》广为人知 今天仍有不少人对此感兴趣

sentences.en: So, how many Instagram posts can you currently find under the hashtag 'declutter'?
sentences.zh: 有多少Instagram 文章目前您在标签“ 剪报” 下能找到?

sentences.en: Is it: a) 2.6 thousand, b) 2.6 million, or c) 26 million?
Hmm, I'm going to go in the middle and say b) 2.6 million.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我要去 中间说b)260万。

sentences.en: OK. We'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: OK,我们到节目结束时会找出答案

sentences.en: As well as social media, decluttering has become popular with television shows, including the BBC's Interior Design Masters.
sentences.zh: 包括英国广播公司的内部设计大师。

sentences.en: Here, one of the show's judges, Michelle Ogundehin, tells BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour why she thinks clutter is such a problem: Visual clutter is more exhausting than we realise.
sentences.zh: 节目中的一位评委Michelle Ogundehin告诉BBC电台四号节目的“女人一小时”,

sentences.en: It's not just stuff. Our brains are constantly processing our surroundings, so they have to work overtime if they're surrounded by chaos.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑在不断处理周围环境, 所以如果周围是一片混乱,他们必须加班。

sentences.en: So, if you feel drained or exhausted at home, it could be your clutter.
sentences.zh: 所以,如果你觉得 排水或疲惫在家里, 它可能是你的杂乱。

sentences.en: I mean, we know that homily 'clear space, clear mind'.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是,我们知道 友好的"清晰的空间,清晰的头脑"。

sentences.en: And I promise you that when you clear away the stuff that has no purpose in your life, you will feel better, lighter, uplifted, energised!
sentences.zh: 我答应你,当你清除的东西 没有目的在你的生活中, 你会感觉更好, 更轻, 提升, 紧张!

sentences.en: In a cluttered room, our brains work overtime, meaning they work extra hard to make sense of the disorder, leaving us exhausted.
sentences.zh: 在一个乱七八糟的房间, 我们的大脑加班, 这意味着他们特别努力工作 来理解混乱, 使我们筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: Work overtime also often means work longer than your set hours.
sentences.zh: 加班也往往意味着工作时间超过规定的时间。

sentences.en: Getting rid of clutter makes us feel uplifted – cheerful, happy and more positive.
sentences.zh: 摆脱混乱使我们感到振奋 — — 欢乐、快乐和更加积极。

sentences.en: It sounds simple, doesn't it? And there's even an expression in English: 'clear space, clear mind'.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很简单,不是吗?英语里甚至有一句话: “清晰的空间,清晰的头脑”。

sentences.en: So, why do many of us find it hard to throw stuff away, even things we rarely use?
sentences.zh: 那么,为什么我们许多人 发现很难扔掉的东西, 甚至我们很少使用的东西?

sentences.en: One reason people put off decluttering is the time it takes.
sentences.zh: 人们推迟消沉的一个原因是它需要时间。

sentences.en: Plus, it can be emotionally disturbing deciding what to keep and what to throw away.
sentences.zh: 再说了,决定保留什么和丢掉什么会让人心烦意乱

sentences.en: But don't worry, says professional organiser and host of The Declutter Club podcast, Ingrid Jansen.
sentences.zh: 但别担心 专业组织者 以及德洛特俱乐部播客 Ingrid Jansen的主持人

sentences.en: The answer is to go slow, as she explains here to BBC Radio 4's Woman's Hour: You have to do decluttering slowly but surely: one drawer, one cupboard at a time.
sentences.zh: 答案是慢一点,正如她在这里向BBC电台4的“女性一小时”解释的那样:你必须缓慢但肯定:一个抽屉,一个柜子一次。

sentences.en: You can't go in all guns blazing. You can't go… and that's what we hear all the time: "This weekend, I'm going to sort out my whole room of doom." And after two hours in, they will look around and go, "What have I done?
sentences.zh: 你不能走光所有的枪。你不能走... 这就是我们一直听到的: “这个周末,我要整理出我整个末日的房间。” 过了两个小时,他们就会四处看看,“我做了什么?”

sentences.en: There's more chaos than there was before!" because they've bitten off [too much that] more than they can chew.
sentences.zh: 混乱比以前多!" 因为他们咬断了[太多] 超过它们能嚼的。

sentences.en: When it comes to decluttering your home, it's best to do things slowly but surely – in a gradual but reliable way which will achieve the result you want.
sentences.zh: 以渐进但可靠的方式实现你想要的结果。

sentences.en: It's a mistake to try to declutter everything all at once, with all guns blazing – an idiom meaning to do things dramatically, with lots of energy and enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 试图同时把一切都弄得乱七八糟, 火力四射, 是一种戏剧性的行为, 充满活力和热情。

sentences.en: After an hour or two of this, decluttering becomes physically and emotionally exhausting.
sentences.zh: 过了一两个小时后 消沉会变得身心疲惫

sentences.en: You may have bitten off more than you can chew – another idiom meaning to try doing something which is too difficult for you.
sentences.zh: 你可能咬得比嚼得还多, 另一回事是尝试做一些对你来说太困难的事情。

sentences.en: So, if you want to declutter without stress, remember: break the job down, and go slow.
sentences.zh: 所以,如果你想无压力地分解, 记住: 打破工作, 慢慢走。

sentences.en: Right, it's time to reveal the answer to my question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 好了 是时候揭开我的问题了 Georgie

sentences.en: I asked you how many Instagram posts you can currently find under the hashtag 'declutter'.
sentences.zh: 我问你现在在标签“delutter”下可以找到多少Instagram 文章。

sentences.en: I said b) 2.6 million. Well, you were correct.
sentences.zh: 我说b) 260万 你说得对

sentences.en: Well done! Yay! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned in this episode about clutter – things we buy which fill up our homes in an untidy, disorganised way.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下我们在这个关于混乱的事件中学到的词汇——我们买的东西以混乱、无组织的方式填满了我们的家园。

sentences.en: When something has to work overtime, it works extra hard using lots of energy.
sentences.zh: 当有东西需要加班时,它会用大量能量来额外地工作。

sentences.en: Work overtime also often means work longer than your set hours.
sentences.zh: 加班也往往意味着工作时间超过规定的时间。

sentences.en: The adjective uplifted means feeling cheerful, happy and optimistic.
sentences.zh: 提振的形容词意味着感到快乐、快乐和乐观。

sentences.en: If you do something slowly but surely, you do it in a gradual but reliable way which will achieve the result you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你做一些缓慢但肯定的事情,你这样做的方式是渐进的,但可靠,从而取得你想要的结果。

sentences.en: The idiom, with all guns blazing, describes doing things with lots of energy and enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 充满火力的智商 描述着用大量精力和热情做的事情

sentences.en: And finally, if you bite off more than you can chew,you try to do something which is too difficult for you.
sentences.zh: 最后,如果你咬得比嚼得还要多, 你就会尝试做一些对你来说太困难的事情。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz for this episode?
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟已经到了, 但为什么不去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 尝试这个插曲的测验?

sentences.en: Good luck decluttering and see you again soon.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运 很快再见

sentences.en: Goodbye! Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见 再见
